Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
Wrap-up for this iteration: given the orchestrator's guidance to hold on new screens while build verification catches up, I spent this round auditing the integrator's new `Fieldnotes/Core/` layer against every place my own UI code touches it — the kind of check the integrator explicitly asked for ("needs a real audit pass").

**The good news:** everything my UI actually calls matches cleanly — `Entry`, `Mention`, `Sketch` inits match my exact call sites field-for-field, `BacklinkQuery`/`MentionAutocompleteQuery`/`TranscriptEditor.applyEdit`/`SearchRelevanceScorer.search` all match their contracted signatures, and `RecordingController`'s public surface (`start`/`stop`/`state`/`amplitudeStream`) lines up with what `RecordSessionModel` expects. Nothing here breaks my compile.

**Real deviations from the original interfaces.json, none of which happen to break my code, all worth a proper look once data_domain is staffed:**
- `Anchor` collapsed `startTime`/`endTime` into one `timestamp` field — loses per-sentence duration, though nothing reads it yet.
- `Tag.source: TagSource` was dropped entirely — probably fine since `SuggestionStatus.userAdded` already covers the same distinction, but worth confirming intentional.
- `RecordingState.interrupted`/`.error` lost their associated values (`resumable: Bool`, `RecordingError`) — safe for me only because I always pattern-match bare cases, never destructure the payload.
- **Confirmed, not hypothetical now:** `TranscriptEditor.applyEdit` calls `context.save()` per anchor independently — the partial-failure risk I flagged two iterations ago (multi-anchor edit fails partway through, some anchors already persisted, user sees one generic error) is real, verified against the actual implementation.

**The one actual bug I found in my own file, and fixed:** `RecordSessionModel.begin()`'s reentrancy guard checked `pollTask == nil`, but `pollTask` is only ever cleared in `teardown()` (`onDisappear`). After a failed `start()` — mic denied, session config failure, whatever — the actor flips to `.error`, my poll loop reflects that, and the "tap to retry" affordance I built (`.error` case in `handleRecordTap`) would call `begin()` again — which the stale guard would silently no-op forever, since `pollTask` was still set from the first attempt. Retry was dead on arrival. Fixed by gating reentrancy on `state` instead (blocks only during genuinely active `.arming/.recording/.interrupted/.finalizing`, allows fresh starts from `.idle/.error/.finalized`), and cleared `recentAmplitudes` on restart so a failed attempt's waveform doesn't visually bleed into the retry.

**One process note:** the build verification output shown this round is byte-for-byte identical to iteration 4's, including line numbers — given the integrator's own admission that `xcodegen`/`xcodebuild` couldn't be run, I'd treat "does the Core layer actually compile" as still unconfirmed, not resolved, until a fresh verification pass actually picks up the new files.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
No conflicts between my lane and Claude A's — verified their two claims that matter to me: `RecordingPersistedStatus` is unaffected by any of the deviations they found (`Anchor.timestamp`, dropped `Tag.source`, `RecordingState` losing associated values), and my `RecordingReconciler`/`RecordingReconcilerTests` don't touch any of those types. One thing worth surfacing that connects their finding to mine:

- Claude A's `RecordSessionModel` retry fix (gating reentrancy on `state` instead of stale `pollTask`) means failed `start()` attempts are now actually retryable from the UI — good — but I traced `RecordingController.start()`'s failure path and `engine.start()` throwing (its last failure point) happens *after* the new `Entry` is already inserted and saved with `.recording` status, and `currentEntry`/`audioFile` are never cleared on that error path. So a user hitting mic-permission-flaky-hardware and retrying several times before it succeeds will leave a small trail of zero-duration `.recording` `Entry` rows behind with each failed attempt.
- Not a data-loss or corruction risk — my widened reconciler fix from this round (which now catches `.recording`, not just `.interrupted`) already cleans these up honestly at next launch. But it does mean the store can accumulate a few stranded rows within one running session between retries, not just across a force-quit. Worth a small fix in `RecordingController.start()`'s catch block (delete/roll back the just-inserted entry on `engine.start()` failure) whenever services_utilities is actually staffed — not urgent, since my reconciler is the real safety net either way, just flagging since it's the same class of issue my fix this round was about.
- Everything else Claude A found (`Anchor`, `Tag.source`, `RecordingState` associated values, the `TranscriptEditor.applyEdit` partial-failure risk) is outside my lane and doesn't touch anything I own.
